narrative.title: Squeezing Repeat SKUs out of a Sorted Rail
narrative.scenario: An inventory rail is value-sorted, but a scanner glitch booked the same SKU several times in a row. Operations wants exactly one entry per distinct SKU, first occurrence kept, and the two-way links re-fused so the rail stays coherent. Because duplicates can only be adjacent in a sorted run, a single forward pass that remembers the value of the last kept entry is enough to squeeze out every repeat.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of n node values forming a doubly linked list sorted in non-decreasing order.
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the list after all duplicate nodes are unlinked, read from the head.

testCases.explanation: The run of three 1s collapses to its first occurrence; the sorted tail is untouched.
Three separate duplicate runs each squeeze down to a single entry.

hintLevels: Level 1: Sorted input means duplicates are always neighbours — no hashing needed.
Level 2: Keep the value of the last surviving node; peel off every following node that equals it, re-fusing prev/next around each removal.
Level 3: Maintain both link directions on every removal (survivor's next and the incoming node's prev) so the rail never loses a backward pointer mid-pass.
